clarification_questions.question: What ethanol level do you need to measure, and over what range during fermentation?

clarification_questions.question: How clear is the wine during fermentation (clear, turbid or opaque), and does it contain solids or CO2 bubbles?

clarification_questions.question: What are the temperature, pressure and fouling conditions in the tank, and how much does the wine composition vary between batches?

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The cited S01 p.12 only says Raman spectra can be used to build chemometric calibration or classification models and that the signal is linear with concentration. It does not say that calibration models are required for this wine or that none exist yet. The status claim about the wine is not in the source. Fix: State only that S01 p.12 says Raman spectra can be used to construct chemometric calibration or classification models, and mark the absence of wine-specific models as an open item to verify rather than a source finding.

overstated: The claim says transmission 'suits clear liquids only'. S01 p.18 says transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate, and that a transflection probe can work for some milk products. 'Only' and 'clear' are not in the source. Fix: Replace with: S01 p.18 states transmission is preferred for transparent or semi-transparent liquids and fails when the sample is too thick or opaque, so wine geometry should be chosen after checking its clarity.

not_supported: S02 p.6 gives transmission ranges for silica fibers (UV-VIS 190-1200 nm, VIS-NIR 350-2400 nm) and IR fibers, but it does not mention Raman at all. The statement that silica fibers suit Raman is therefore not in the cited page. Fix: Limit the fiber statement to what S02 p.6 shows: silica fibers cover UV-VIS and VIS-NIR, and IR fibers cover the mid-IR range. If Raman fiber use is mentioned, cite S01 p.18 (Raman probe in the multispectral milk setup, 785 nm excitation) or S01 p.11 (Raman probes of special design) instead.

not_supported: S01 p.10 covers ATR fiber probes and NIR diffuse reflection and chemometrics in general. It does not say that a calibration built on one wine type will fail for other wines. Fix: Cite S01 p.12 for the general point that Raman and IR spectra support chemometric calibration models, and present the wine-type transfer risk as a reasoned inference that needs validation rather than as a source statement.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [guidance]
raman_fluorescence_background: Raman can be swamped by fluorescence background from many organic compounds; check signal quality first. [S01 p.11]

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
